strings.d1.theme: Old City: Jewish and Christian quarters
strings.d1.s0.name: Western Wall
strings.d1.s0.tips: Enter via Jaffa Gate. The Western Wall is open 24 hours, with separate men's and women's sections; men must cover their heads (kippahs are provided). On Friday evening there is a Shabbat welcome.
strings.d1.s1.name: Temple Mount Dome of the Rock
strings.d1.s1.tips: Non-Muslims can visit Sunday to Thursday 07:30-11:00 and 13:30-14:30 (via the Mughrabi Bridge). Admire the Dome of the Rock from the outside. Modest dress is required; closed Friday and Saturday.
strings.d1.s2.name: Via Dolorosa
strings.d1.s2.tips: The 14 Stations of the Cross, from the Lions' Gate to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre. On Fridays at 15:00 a Franciscan procession passes through.
strings.d1.s3.name: Church of the Holy Sepulchre
strings.d1.s3.tips: The site of Jesus's crucifixion and tomb. Climb the steps to Golgotha, expect a queue for the Edicule, and note that six denominations share the church.
strings.d1.s4.name: Abu Shukri Via Dolorosa
strings.d1.s4.tips: The Old City's legendary hummus, plus ful (fava bean stew) and falafel.
strings.d1.b0.name: Lina Restaurant Old City
strings.d1.b0.tips: Hummus in the Christian Quarter, and Abu Shukri's rival.
strings.d1.b1.name: Tower of David Museum
strings.d1.b1.tips: A citadel museum with panoramic views from the ramparts. An alternative to the Via Dolorosa.
strings.d2.theme: Mount of Olives and City of David
strings.d2.s0.name: Mount of Olives Viewpoint
strings.d2.s0.tips: Take a taxi up. The Old City and the golden dome look best in morning light. Pass the Jewish cemetery, then walk down.
strings.d2.s1.name: Church of All Nations Gethsemane
strings.d2.s1.tips: Olive trees over 2,000 years old stand in the Garden of Gethsemane. On the way, stop at Dominus Flevit (the Church of the Teardrop).
strings.d2.s2.name: City of David
strings.d2.s2.tips: Excavations of King David's original city. Choose Hezekiah's Tunnel (knee-deep water, bring a torch) or the dry Canaanite Tunnel.
strings.d2.s3.name: Ja'far Sweets
strings.d2.s3.tips: Try knafeh (cheese pastry soaked in syrup). Pass through the Damascus Gate market in the Muslim Quarter.
strings.d2.s4.name: Ramparts Walk
strings.d2.s4.tips: Walk the top of the city walls from Jaffa Gate to Lions' Gate, with views over rooftops and domes.
strings.d2.b0.name: Azzahra Restaurant East Jerusalem
strings.d2.b0.tips: Palestinian cooking in East Jerusalem; try the maqluba (upside-down rice dish).
strings.d2.b1.name: Garden Tomb
strings.d2.b1.tips: The Protestant alternative to the Holy Sepulchre: a peaceful garden outside Damascus Gate.
strings.d3.theme: Yad Vashem and the Israel Museum
strings.d3.s0.name: Yad Vashem
strings.d3.s0.tips: The Holocaust memorial museum, with Safdie's prism-shaped building and the Children's Memorial. Free; book online. Children under 10 are not admitted. Closed Saturday.
strings.d3.s1.name: Israel Museum
strings.d3.s1.tips: See the Dead Sea Scrolls (Shrine of the Book), a model of Jerusalem in the Second Temple period, and the archaeology galleries. Lunch at the cafeteria.
strings.d3.s2.name: Israel Museum Modern Kafe
strings.d3.s2.tips: The museum restaurant, with a garden overlooking the Dead Sea.
strings.d3.s3.name: Knesset
strings.d3.s3.tips: See the parliament building from outside, plus the Menorah sculpture. Tours run on Sundays and Thursdays.
strings.d3.s4.name: Mahane Yehuda Market
strings.d3.s4.tips: The shuk is a market by day and a street of bars by night. Try the marzipan rugelach, kubbeh at Azura, and Hachapuria.
strings.d3.b0.name: Machneyuda Restaurant
strings.d3.b0.tips: A chef's restaurant next to the market. Book weeks ahead.
strings.d3.b1.name: Bible Lands Museum
strings.d3.b1.tips: Next door to the Israel Museum, covering the ancient Near East.
strings.d4.s0.name: Masada National Park
strings.d4.s0.tips: Take bus 486 or a tour, 1.5 hours. Herod's rock fortress and the Roman siege ramp; climb the Snake Path for sunrise (in summer, climbing is banned after 08:00; the cable car costs 28 ILS).
strings.d4.s1.name: Ein Gedi Nature Reserve
strings.d4.s1.tips: It reaches 40°C in summer. Pick the short David Waterfall trail, stay in the shade and carry water.
strings.d4.s2.name: Ein Gedi Kibbutz Restoranı
strings.d4.s2.tips: A kibbutz canteen or a beach café.
strings.d4.s3.name: Ein Bokek Dead Sea Beach
strings.d4.s3.tips: The lowest point on Earth (-430 m). Swim, float on the water, apply the mud and protect your eyes. Free public beach with showers.
strings.d4.b0.name: Qumran National Park
strings.d4.b0.tips: The caves where the scrolls were found. An alternative to Ein Gedi.
strings.d4.b1.name: Ein Bokek Plaj Kafesi
strings.d4.b1.tips: A beachside café serving salads and lemonade.
strings.d5.s0.name: Church of the Nativity Bethlehem
strings.d5.s0.tips: Take bus 231 or a taxi (Palestinian Authority area; bring your passport, and Israeli-plated cars cannot cross). Visit the cave where Jesus was born; the queue can take 2 hours.
strings.d5.s1.name: Banksy Walled Off Hotel & Separation Wall
strings.d5.s1.tips: Wall graffiti plus Banksy's hotel and museum. Go by taxi.
strings.d5.s2.name: Afteem Restaurant Bethlehem
strings.d5.s3.name: Ein Karem
strings.d5.s3.tips: The village of John the Baptist, with the Church of the Visitation, Mary's Spring and art galleries. It lies west of Jerusalem.
strings.d5.s4.name: Karma Ein Karem
strings.d5.s4.tips: A terrace café with village views. Go in the evening.
strings.d5.b0.name: Shepherds' Field Beit Sahour
strings.d5.b0.tips: The Shepherds' Field church. An alternative to the wall.
strings.d5.b1.name: Sweet N Karem
strings.d5.b1.tips: An ice cream shop in Ein Karem.
strings.d6.s0.name: Yemin Moshe & Montefiore Windmill
strings.d6.s0.tips: The first neighbourhood built outside the walls, with a windmill and views of the Old City.
strings.d6.s1.name: First Station Jerusalem
strings.d6.s1.tips: A former Ottoman railway station with cafés, a market and a children's area.
strings.d6.s2.name: Azura Mahane Yehuda
strings.d6.s2.tips: Kurdish-Iraqi dishes such as kubbeh and aubergine. Expect crowds before Shabbat.
strings.d6.s3.name: Mea Shearim
strings.d6.s3.tips: An ultra-Orthodox neighbourhood. Dress modestly, don't take photos, and expect the Friday rush before Shabbat.
strings.d6.s4.name: Western Wall Shabbat Welcome
strings.d6.s4.tips: On Friday at sunset there is singing and dancing (no photos). On other days, evening prayers.
strings.d6.b0.name: Anna Italian Café Ticho House
strings.d6.b0.tips: A garden restaurant in the historic Ticho House.
strings.d6.b1.name: Hebrew University Mount Scopus
strings.d6.b1.tips: A botanical garden with desert views. An alternative to Mea Shearim.
strings.d7.theme: Armenian Quarter and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Armenian Quarter
strings.d7.s0.tips: St James's Cathedral (service at 15:00) and ceramics workshops.
strings.d7.s1.name: Cardo Jewish Quarter
strings.d7.s1.tips: Remains of the Byzantine-era main street. The Hurva Synagogue offers dome views for 20 ILS.
strings.d7.s2.name: Rooftop Promenade Old City
strings.d7.s2.tips: Rooftops above the bazaar, where four quarters meet. Free.
strings.d7.s3.name: Hummus Ben Sira
strings.d7.s3.tips: West Jerusalem hummus for a farewell meal.
strings.d7.s4.name: Jerusalem Navon Station
strings.d7.s4.tips: The high-speed train to Ben Gurion takes 25 minutes (not running on Shabbat). A farewell to the city.
strings.d7.b0.name: Jerusalem Armenian Ceramics
strings.d7.b1.name: Tmol Shilshom
strings.note0: Get a Rav-Kav card and use the light rail (Jaffa Street). On Shabbat (Friday sunset to Saturday night) public transport and most shops are closed, but Arab East Jerusalem stays open. The Ben Gurion high-speed train takes 25 minutes.
strings.note1: Summer is 30°C and dry, with cool nights. The Dead Sea and Masada reach 40°C, so go at sunrise. Wear suitable clothing for the Temple Mount and carry water.
strings.note2: SAFETY: The situation in the region is changeable, so check official advisories before you travel. Temple Mount hours may change or the site may close. Go to Bethlehem by taxi or bus (Israeli-plated rental cars cannot enter).
strings.note3: Dress code at holy sites: shoulders and knees covered, and men must cover their heads at the Wall. The Temple Mount is closed Friday and Saturday; Yad Vashem is closed Saturday.
strings.note4: Hummus costs 40-60 ILS, falafel 20, a restaurant meal 100-150; tip 12%. Cards are accepted everywhere; carry cash in East Jerusalem.
strings.note5: Tap water is safe to drink. Mahane Yehuda is liveliest on Friday afternoon.
